children: Global pension capital investor IFM Investors, which has A$291.6 billion ($209.9 billion) in assets under management, opened a Singapore office on Thursday as it aims to deepen its private market footprint in Asia.
IFM said the Singapore office will support the expansion of its private market operations across the region, especially in diversified credit, through local origination and execution.
The firm is looking to pursue investment opportunities and attract institutional capital across markets throughout Asia.

"Asia is viewed as an increasingly important growth market for institutional capital - including pension capital, sovereign wealth funds, insurers - supported by relatively under penetrated private markets, rising demand for flexible finance solutions, and growing investor interest for diversification," IFM said in a press release.

IFM is owned by 15 Australian industry superannuation funds and one UK pension fund. The firm serves more than 880 institutional investors worldwide and operates from 18 offices across Australia, Europe, North America and Asia.

"Asia-Pacific private credit is at an inflection point, with the market growing nearly fourfold from a low base over the past 15 years," said Hiran Wanigasekera, IFM's executive director and co-head of APAC diversified credit.
